<thought>The observed isotopic envelope shows a series of peaks spaced by 1 Da from the monoisotopic mass, with relative intensities that follow the binomial distribution expected for 13C (≈1.1 % natural abundance) in a molecule containing ~16 C atoms. No other common element produces such a multi‑peak pattern; chlorine, bromine, sulfur, etc., give only one or two characteristic peaks. Therefore, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
